skill.name: conductor-validator
skill.description: Validates Conductor project artifacts for completeness, consistency, and correctness. Use after setup, when diagnosing issues, or before implementation to verify project context.
skill.summary: Validates Conductor project structure, required files, status markers, task markers, and track identifiers.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static alerts were false positives from Markdown code fences, inline resource text, and [~] status markers. The explicit Bash usage is read-only local ls inspection of Conductor paths, with no dynamic input, network activity, or destructive behavior.

remediation.issue: Read-only Bash checks may trigger external command warnings.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer Read, Glob, and Grep instructions for directory checks, or state that Bash commands are optional and read-only.

content.value_statement: Conductor projects can drift when tracks, plans, and required files are missing. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused checks for project readiness.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether the conductor directory exists.
Checks whether conductor track directories are present.
Checks for required Conductor documents such as index, product, tech stack, workflow, and tracks files.
Documents expected track status markers for not started, in progress, and complete states.
Documents expected task markers in plan files.
Defines the expected track identifier pattern with type, name, and date parts.
limitations: It only describes checks for Conductor project structures.
It does not provide a complete Conductor specification.
It relies on repository contents available to the assistant.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Setup Validation
use_cases.description: Confirm a new Conductor workspace includes the required directory, core documents, and track index before work starts.

use_cases.title: Track Review
use_cases.description: Check track names, progress markers, and task markers before sharing project status.

use_cases.title: Implementation Readiness
use_cases.description: Review project context before coding so missing product, workflow, or technical documents are found early.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the Conductor setup in this repository. Check for the conductor directory, track directory, and required top-level documents.

prompt_templates.title: Review Status Markers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review conductor tracks and plan files for valid status markers. Summarize missing or inconsistent markers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Track Identifiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit Conductor track identifiers against the expected type, name, and date pattern. Report names that need correction.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Before implementation, validate Conductor artifacts for completeness and consistency. Prioritize blockers, missing context, and unclear track progress.

output_examples.input: Validate a new Conductor workspace before planning begins.
output_examples.output: The review confirms the main Conductor directory and required documents. It flags the missing tracks directory as a setup blocker.

output: One track is in progress and two tracks are complete.
One plan has pending tasks without a matching track status.
The report recommends updating the track summary before coding starts.

best_practices: Run the validator after setup and before major implementation work.
Keep track status markers and task status markers consistent across files.
Review reported gaps before using Conductor context for coding decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for projects that do not use Conductor artifacts.
Do not treat missing required documents as harmless when planning implementation.
Do not modify project files before separating validation findings from fixes.

faq.question: What does this skill validate?
faq.answer: It checks Conductor directories, required documents, status markers, task markers, and track identifier patterns.

faq.question: Does it change files?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes validation checks and reporting steps, not automatic edits.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I run it?
faq.answer: Run it after setup, during issue diagnosis, or before implementation starts.

faq.question: Does it validate every project convention?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on the Conductor structure and marker patterns described in the skill.

faq.question: Can it replace a project review?
faq.answer: No. It helps find missing artifacts, but humans should decide project readiness.
